1726	    def _bilevel_step_autograd(self, model, val_x, val_y, criterion,
1727	                               meta_optimizer, named_params, saved_grads,
1728	                               param_info, mn):
1729	        """Autograd fallback path for bilevel_step."""
1730	        meta_optimizer.zero_grad()
1731	        smart_grads = {}
1732	        new_gru_states = {}
1733	        with torch.enable_grad():
1734	            for (name, p, pidx, grad_flat, sharp_flat) in param_info:
1735	                gru_state = self._flat_gru_states[pidx].float()
1736	                smart_grad, new_gru, _f, _b = mn.forward_for_bilevel(
1737	                    grad_flat, sharp_flat, gru_state)
1738	                smart_grads[name] = smart_grad
1739	                new_gru_states[pidx] = new_gru.detach()
1740	
1741	        model.zero_grad()
1742	        with torch.enable_grad():
1743	            val_loss = criterion(model(val_x), val_y)
1744	            val_loss.backward()
1745	
1746	        grad_outputs = []
1747	        outputs = []
1748	        for (name, p, pidx, grad_flat, sharp_flat) in param_info:
1749	            if p.grad is None:
1750	                continue
1751	            # Sanitize the val-grad on-device instead of an
1752	            # ``isfinite(vg).all()`` reduction-to-host skip: zero any NaN/Inf
1753	            # entries (no-op when already finite). nan_to_num maps a fully
1754	            # non-finite grad to all-zeros, whose norm is 0 -> the existing
1755	            # ``vg_norm > 1e-12`` branch then leaves vg_unit at zero, i.e. no
1756	            # contribution, matching the old skip semantics in that case.
1757	            vg = torch.nan_to_num(
1758	                p.grad.detach().reshape(-1).float(),
1759	                nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
1760	            vg_norm = vg.norm()
1761	            vg_unit = vg / vg_norm if vg_norm > 1e-12 else vg
1762	            sg = smart_grads[name].reshape(-1)
1763	            outputs.append(sg)
1764	            grad_outputs.append(-vg_unit)
1765	
1766	        if outputs:
1767	            torch.autograd.backward(outputs, grad_outputs)
1768	
1769	        if self.bilevel_allreduce_meta_grads:
1770	            self._allreduce_meta_grads()
1771	
1772	        meta_optimizer.step()
1773	        self._weights_dirty = True
1774	
1775	        for pidx, ng in new_gru_states.items():
1776	            self._flat_gru_states[pidx] = ng
1777	
1778	        for name, p in named_params:
1779	            p.grad = saved_grads.get(name)
1780	
1781	        return val_loss.detach()

123	// A CUDA build links ONLY sg::sm90 symbols; a HIP build ONLY sg::gfx942. A
124	// `case` that calls the other arch's namespace is an undefined symbol that
125	// makes the .so fail to load (e.g. sg::gfx942::moe_filter_active_params in a
126	// CUDA-only build — the gfx942 .hip TUs are never compiled by nvcc). Gate each
127	// case by its backend macro, mirroring dispatch.cpp's WITH_CUDA/WITH_HIP split,
128	// so the Python front-end binds exactly the backend that was compiled in.
129	// (WITH_HIP wins if both are somehow defined, matching dispatch.cpp.)
130	#if defined(WITH_CUDA) && !defined(WITH_HIP)
131	#  define SG_CASE_SM90_RET(METHOD, ...)  case 90:  return ::sg::sm90::METHOD(__VA_ARGS__);
132	#  define SG_CASE_SM90_CALL(METHOD, ...) case 90:  ::sg::sm90::METHOD(__VA_ARGS__); break;
133	#else
134	#  define SG_CASE_SM90_RET(METHOD, ...)
135	#  define SG_CASE_SM90_CALL(METHOD, ...)
136	#endif
137	#if defined(WITH_HIP)
138	#  define SG_CASE_GFX942_RET(METHOD, ...)  case 942: return ::sg::gfx942::METHOD(__VA_ARGS__);
139	#  define SG_CASE_GFX942_CALL(METHOD, ...) case 942: ::sg::gfx942::METHOD(__VA_ARGS__); break;

141	#  define SG_CASE_GFX942_RET(METHOD, ...)
142	#  define SG_CASE_GFX942_CALL(METHOD, ...)
143	#endif

147	    do { \
148	        const int sg_arch_ = ::sg::detect_arch(); \

175	// ── Boundary validation for optimizer fused-step entrypoints ─────────
176	// The Python wrappers historically owned device/dtype/shape/contiguity
177	// invariants; these binding entrypoints trusted them. A non-contiguous param
178	// view, a device/dtype mismatch between param and grad, or a shape mismatch
179	// silently corrupts the in-place fused update (the launchers index a flat
180	// pointer with the param's numel). Validate at the C++ boundary so a bad call
181	// fails loudly. `where` is the entrypoint name for the error message.
182	//
183	// We check the param against its paired grad. Optimizer-state buffers (m, v,
184	// ema, …) are allocated by the wrapper from `torch.zeros_like(param)` so they
185	// inherit the param's device/dtype/shape/contiguity; the param check is the
186	// load-bearing one. A missing/empty grad (sparse-grad fallback) is skipped —
187	// the per-op loops already filter those out before dispatch.
188	inline void check_param_grad(
189	    const torch::Tensor& p,
190	    const torch::Tensor& g,
191	    const char* where
192	) {
193	    TORCH_CHECK(p.defined(), where, ": param tensor is undefined");
194	#if defined(WITH_HIP)
195	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_hip(), where, ": param must be on a HIP device");
196	#else
197	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_cuda(), where, ": param must be on a CUDA device");
198	#endif
199	    // A non-contiguous param view aliases a strided storage; the fused
200	    // launchers treat data_ptr() as a dense [numel] buffer, so a strided view
201	    // would read/write the wrong elements and silently corrupt the update.
202	    TORCH_CHECK(p.is_contiguous(), where,
203	                ": param must be contiguous (got a non-contiguous view); "
204	                "call .contiguous() in the Python wrapper before the fused step");
205	    if (!g.defined() || g.numel() == 0) return;  // sparse-grad: skip (filtered)
206	    TORCH_CHECK(g.device() == p.device(), where,
207	                ": grad device (", g.device().str(),
208	                ") != param device (", p.device().str(), ")");
209	    TORCH_CHECK(g.scalar_type() == p.scalar_type(), where,
210	                ": grad dtype (", toString(g.scalar_type()),
211	                ") != param dtype (", toString(p.scalar_type()), ")");
212	    TORCH_CHECK(g.sizes() == p.sizes(), where,
213	                ": grad shape (", g.sizes(), ") != param shape (",
214	                p.sizes(), ")");
215	    TORCH_CHECK(g.is_contiguous(), where, ": grad must be contiguous");
216	}

218	// Validate every (param, grad) pair in a multi-tensor fused-step entrypoint.
219	inline void check_params_grads(
220	    const std::vector<torch::Tensor>& params,
221	    const std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
222	    const char* where
223	) {
224	    TORCH_CHECK(params.size() == grads.size(), where,
225	                ": params.size() (", params.size(),
226	                ") != grads.size() (", grads.size(), ")");
227	    for (size_t i = 0; i < params.size(); ++i)
228	        check_param_grad(params[i], grads[i], where);
229	}

231	// ── Secondary-list length guard for multi-tensor entrypoints ─────────
232	// check_params_grads validates the PRIMARY (params, grads) pairing. A
233	// multi-tensor fused step also receives several SECONDARY parallel lists
234	// (exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, emas, mus, slows, gru_states, sharpness caches, per-
235	// param step counters, per-layer scalar vectors, …). The launchers index those
236	// lists by the same i used for params[i], so a short/long secondary list either
237	// reads out of bounds or silently pairs the wrong buffer with a param — the same
238	// class of silent corruption check_param_grad guards against, but on the state
239	// side. Validate each secondary list's length == the expected element count.
240	//
241	// `what` names the offending list, `fn` the entrypoint, both in the message.
242	// A templated overload covers the scalar vectors (std::vector<float/int64_t/
243	// double>) so the SuperGrok per-layer alpha/beta1/step vectors are guarded too.
244	inline void check_list_len(
245	    const std::vector<torch::Tensor>& v,
246	    size_t expect,
247	    const char* what,
248	    const char* fn
249	) {
250	    TORCH_CHECK(v.size() == expect, fn, ": ", what, " list length (", v.size(),
251	                ") != expected (", expect, ") — every secondary list must be "
252	                "the same length as params/grads; the launcher indexes them in "
253	                "lockstep.");
254	}

258	    const std::vector<Scalar>& v,
259	    size_t expect,
260	    const char* what,
261	    const char* fn
262	) {
263	    TORCH_CHECK(v.size() == expect, fn, ": ", what, " list length (", v.size(),
264	                ") != expected (", expect, ") — every secondary list must be "
265	                "the same length as params/grads; the launcher indexes them in "
266	                "lockstep.");
267	}

269	// ── Device-side gradient clipping: single CPU sync instead of N ──────
270	inline void clip_grad_norms_device_side(
271	    std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
272	    size_t n_params,
273	    float grad_clip_norm
274	) {
275	    if (grad_clip_norm <= 0.0f) return;
276	
277	    // Collect the present grads once. Fused multi-tensor ops want a flat list.
278	    std::vector<torch::Tensor> present;
279	    present.reserve(n_params);
280	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_params; i++) {
281	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0)
282	            present.push_back(grads[i]);
283	    }
284	    if (present.empty()) return;
285	
286	    // Per-tensor L2 norms via a single fused multi-tensor reduction
287	    // (torch::_foreach_norm), replacing the per-tensor upcast + dot + add_
288	    // (≈2N kernel launches) with one foreach launch. Numerics: the L2 norm of
289	    // each tensor is accumulated into a fp32 sum-of-squares (squaring the
290	    // per-tensor norm == that tensor's sum-of-squares), matching the original
291	    // fp32 accumulation of the global sum-of-squares. To preserve the original
292	    // precision when grads are NOT already fp32, upcast those (only) to fp32
293	    // before the norm; fp32 grads skip the upcast entirely.
294	    bool all_fp32 = true;
295	    for (auto& g : present)
296	        if (g.scalar_type() != torch::kFloat32) { all_fp32 = false; break; }
297	
298	    std::vector<torch::Tensor> norm_inputs;
299	    if (all_fp32) {
300	        norm_inputs = present;
301	    } else {
302	        norm_inputs.reserve(present.size());
303	        for (auto& g : present)
304	            norm_inputs.push_back(g.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32
305	                                      ? g
306	                                      : g.to(torch::kFloat32));
307	    }
308	
309	    auto norms = torch::_foreach_norm(norm_inputs, /*p=*/2);
310	    // norm_sq = sum_i (||g_i||_2)^2, accumulated in fp32 on-device, one sync.
311	    auto stacked = torch::stack(norms).to(torch::kFloat32);
312	    float total_norm =
313	        std::sqrt(stacked.dot(stacked).item<float>());
314	
315	    if (total_norm > grad_clip_norm) {
316	        float clip_coef = grad_clip_norm / (total_norm + 1e-6f);
317	        // Fused multi-tensor in-place scale of the present grads.
318	        torch::_foreach_mul_(present, clip_coef);
319	    }
320	}
321	
322	// ── Device-side SAM grad-norm: single CPU sync instead of N ──────────
323	inline float compute_sam_grad_norm_device_side(
324	    std::vector<torch::Tensor>& grads,
325	    size_t n_grads
326	) {
327	    torch::Device dev(torch::kCPU);
328	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_grads; i++) {
329	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0) {
330	            dev = grads[i].device();
331	            break;
332	        }
333	    }
334	    auto norm_sq = torch::zeros(
335	        {1}, torch::TensorOptions().device(dev).dtype(torch::kFloat32));
336	    for (size_t i = 0; i < n_grads; i++) {
337	        if (grads[i].defined() && grads[i].numel() > 0) {
338	            auto g_flat = grads[i].to(torch::kFloat32).reshape(-1);
339	            norm_sq.add_(g_flat.dot(g_flat));
340	        }
341	    }
342	    return std::sqrt(norm_sq.item<float>()) + 1e-12f;
343	}

106	// Single integer that versions the SET of exported pybind signatures below
107	// (every m.def's argument list + return type, and the secondary-list/scalar
108	// contracts the Python optimizers rely on). BUMP THIS on ANY exported-signature
109	// change: adding/removing/reordering a fused-step argument, changing a tensor
110	// list into a scalar (or vice-versa), changing a return tuple, or renaming an
111	// exported symbol. A stale prebuilt .so paired with newer Python wrappers (or
112	// the reverse) otherwise mis-marshals arguments silently; a version mismatch
113	// must fail loudly instead.

116	// wrappers were written for) lands SEPARATELY in grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py
117	// (sibling-owned). Until that check exists this attribute is exported but inert
118	// — that is intentional and harmless: it merely makes the version observable
119	// now so the Python guard can be added without a coordinated ABI bump.
120	constexpr int GROK_ABI_SCHEMA = 1;

122	// ── Module name (#12 tuner-JIT fix) ──────────────────────────────────
123	// The module must export the PyInit_<name> of the name it is BUILT as, or the
124	// importing side can never bind it. TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME is supplied by BOTH
125	// build paths:
126	//   • product/AOT: torch's BuildExtension defines it from the last component
127	//     of the extension name ("grokking_optimizers._ops" → _ops), so the
128	//     shipped .so still exports PyInit__ops — identical to the old pinned
129	//     name;

131	//     defines it to the variant module name (grokking_compiled_<opt>_<model>_

133	//     impossible under the old pinned `_ops` (#12: no JIT variant could ever
134	//     import; the autotuner could not time real variants) — now succeeds.

1	// =====================================================================
2	// dispatch.cpp — single-source arch detection + fused_step dispatch
3	//
4	// Arch-honest LOUD-GATE dispatch (Phase 8). The kernel source has real bodies
5	// only for sm_90/sm_90a (one CUDA tree, sg::sm90) and gfx942 (one HIP tree,
6	// sg::gfx942). detect_arch_from_device() therefore returns 90 for NVIDIA
7	// major==9 and 942 for gfx942, and THROWS for any other CC/gfx (e.g. an A100
8	// sm_80, which has no TMA/WGMMA path) rather than silently running Hopper SASS
9	// on the wrong architecture. FORCE_ARCH is the explicit operator override.
10	// TPU arch is handled in Python via JAX.
11	// =====================================================================
12	
13	#include "helpers.h"
14	
15	#include <cstdlib>
16	#include <cstring>
17	#include <limits>
18	#include <stdexcept>
19	#include <string>
20	#include <unordered_map>
21	
22	#if defined(WITH_CUDA) && !defined(WITH_HIP)
23	 #include <cuda_runtime.h>
24	 #include <c10/cuda/CUDAStream.h>
25	#elif defined(WITH_HIP)
26	 #include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
27	 #include <c10/hip/HIPStream.h>
28	#endif
29	
30	namespace sg {
31	
32	namespace {
33	
34	int detect_arch_from_env() {
35	 const char* force = std::getenv("FORCE_ARCH");
36	 if (!force) return -1;
37	 std::string s(force);
38	 // TPU is handled in Python; not valid for C++ dispatch.
39	 if (s.rfind("tpu", 0) == 0) {
40	 throw std::runtime_error(
41	 "FORCE_ARCH=" + s + " is not a GPU arch; TPU dispatch is handled "
42	 "in Python via JAX.");
43	 }
44	 // AMD: any gfx target (and the bare 942 form) -> the gfx942 impl.
45	 if (s == "942" || s.rfind("gfx", 0) == 0) return 942;
46	 // NVIDIA: any sm_* / smXX form -> the sm90 impl.
47	 if (s.rfind("sm_", 0) == 0 || s.rfind("sm", 0) == 0) return 90;
48	 // Bare numeric compute capability (e.g. "70", "90", "120") -> NVIDIA.
49	 if (!s.empty() && s.find_first_not_of("0123456789") == std::string::npos)
50	 return 90;
51	 throw std::runtime_error(
52	 "FORCE_ARCH=" + s +
53	 " not recognized. Use an NVIDIA arch (sm_70..sm_120 or a numeric "
54	 "compute capability), an AMD arch (gfx906..gfx1201), or run TPU via "
55	 "Python/JAX.");
56	}
57	
58	int detect_arch_from_device() {
59	#if defined(WITH_CUDA) && !defined(WITH_HIP)
60	 int dev = 0;
61	 cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
62	 if (err != cudaSuccess) {
63	 throw std::runtime_error(
64	 std::string("cudaGetDevice failed: ") + cudaGetErrorString(err));
65	 }
66	 // Query only the compute-capability attributes (cheap device-attribute
67	 // reads) instead of the full cudaGetDeviceProperties struct copy.
68	 int major = 0, minor = 0;
69	 err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&major, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, dev);
70	 if (err != cudaSuccess) {
71	 throw std::runtime_error(
72	 std::string("cudaDeviceGetAttribute(ComputeCapabilityMajor) failed: ") +
73	 cudaGetErrorString(err));
74	 }
75	 err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&minor, cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMinor, dev);
76	 if (err != cudaSuccess) {
77	 throw std::runtime_error(
78	 std::string("cudaDeviceGetAttribute(ComputeCapabilityMinor) failed: ") +
79	 cudaGetErrorString(err));
80	 }
81	 int sm = major * 10 + minor;
82	 // ARCH-HONEST DISPATCH (Stage 4): route per the REAL compute capability,
83	 // not "any NVIDIA -> 90". The shipped device code has ONE NVIDIA kernel
84	 // BODY: the sm_90a Hopper impl (TMA / wgmma — instructions that do not
85	 // exist on Ampere/Ada). setup.py emits SASS for every CC the toolchain
86	 // accepts plus a PTX fallback, but that PTX is lowered from sm_90a-gated
87	 // source, so it cannot JIT-forward to sm_80/sm_86/sm_89 — an A100 routed
88	 // to the sm_90a path would hit an illegal-instruction fault (or worse,
89	 // undefined behavior), not a clean error.
90	 //
91	 // POLICY: LOUD-GATE. We accept the Hopper family (sm_90 / sm_90a, i.e.
92	 // major == 9) and route it to impl 90. Every other NVIDIA CC fails loudly
93	 // here. This is the truthful option because only sm_90a has a real kernel
94	 // body — there is no sm_80/sm_86/sm_89 impl to route to. If a per-CC body
95	 // is ever added, give it its own selector value and a case here.
96	 if (major == 9) return 90;  // Hopper (sm_90 / sm_90a)
97	 throw std::runtime_error(
98	 "Detected sm_" + std::to_string(sm) +
99	 ": no kernel body for this NVIDIA compute capability. The shipped "
100	 "device code has only the sm_90a (Hopper) body, whose TMA/wgmma "
101	 "instructions are not valid on this arch and cannot be JIT-forwarded "
102	 "from the embedded PTX. Supported: sm_90a (NVIDIA), gfx942 (AMD). "
103	 "Set FORCE_ARCH=sm_90 only on a real Hopper device.");
104	#elif defined(WITH_HIP)
105	 int dev = 0;
106	 hipError_t err = hipGetDevice(&dev);
107	 if (err != hipSuccess) {
108	 throw std::runtime_error(
109	 std::string("hipGetDevice failed: ") + hipGetErrorString(err));
110	 }
111	 hipDeviceProp_t prop;
112	 err = hipGetDeviceProperties(&prop, dev);
113	 if (err != hipSuccess) {
114	 throw std::runtime_error(
115	 std::string("hipGetDeviceProperties failed: ") +
116	 hipGetErrorString(err));
117	 }
118	 std::string arch_name = prop.gcnArchName; // e.g. "gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-"
119	 auto colon = arch_name.find(':');
120	 if (colon != std::string::npos) arch_name = arch_name.substr(0, colon);
121	 // ARCH-HONEST DISPATCH (Stage 4), AMD twin of the NVIDIA loud-gate above.
122	 // The shipped AMD device code has ONE body: the gfx942 (CDNA3) impl. A
123	 // gfx906/gfx908/gfx90a/gfx1100 device routed to the gfx942 code object
124	 // would run an incompatible ISA. setup.py offload-compiles for every gfx
125	 // the toolchain accepts, but the kernel BODY is gfx942-specific, so route
126	 // only a real gfx942 to impl 942 and fail loudly otherwise.
127	 // POLICY: LOUD-GATE (only gfx942 has a body).
128	 if (arch_name == "gfx942") return 942;
129	 throw std::runtime_error(
130	 "Detected " + arch_name +
131	 ": no kernel body for this AMD gfx target. The shipped device code "
132	 "has only the gfx942 (CDNA3 / MI300X) body. Supported: sm_90a "
133	 "(NVIDIA), gfx942 (AMD).");
134	#else
135	 throw std::runtime_error(
136	 "No GPU backend compiled in. Build with WITH_CUDA or WITH_HIP.");
137	#endif
138	}
139	
140	} // anonymous namespace
141	
142	int detect_arch() {
143	 // The GPU arch (and FORCE_ARCH) cannot change mid-process, so resolve it
144	 // exactly once. SG_DISPATCH invokes this up to n_params×ns_steps per step;
145	 // memoizing turns the per-dispatch getenv + device query into a single
146	 // C++11-guaranteed-thread-safe lazy init that subsequent calls read for free.
147	 static const int cached_arch = [] {
148	 int env_arch = detect_arch_from_env();
149	 if (env_arch >= 0) return env_arch;
150	 return detect_arch_from_device();
151	 }();
152	 return cached_arch;
153	}

156	// fused_step — Stage 6 L3 persistent-megakernel dispatch (§1.12)
157	//
158	// PREFERS a fused TU when one is present for (model, optimizer, arch):
159	// the generated csrc/fused/<arch>/ megakernels register a host launcher per
160	// solver-chosen cell. fused_step detects the arch, looks up the cell, and —
161	// if a real fused TU is wired for it — dispatches there; otherwise it throws a

172	#if defined(WITH_CUDA) && !defined(WITH_HIP)
173	namespace fused {
174	// The persistent-megakernel scratch the host zero-initializes (mirror of
175	// csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh::PersistentContext — kept layout-identical).

177	// This MUST live in sg::fused (NOT sg::fused::sm90): the real struct in

186	 int* g_next_task;

192	// FusedScalars mirror — layout-identical to csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh
193	// ::FusedScalars (the FULL runtime scalar set the host binds: lr, beta1, beta2,

201	// types byte-identical to the real struct — fused_step memcpy-fills this and the
202	// cell reads it positionally via apply_scalars().
203	namespace sm90 {
204	struct FusedScalars {
205	 float lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, alpha, beta, lamb, alpha_max,
206	       gate, d_factor, neg_lr_scale, decay_factor,
207	       // GrokAdamW append-only widening (decoder L3-TC) — keep in lock-step with
208	       // the real fused::sm90::FusedScalars (opt_components.cuh). Inert defaults
209	       // (0.0) for every non-GrokAdamW caller; layout stays byte-identical.
210	       gamma, grad_clip,
211	       // Prodigy append-only widening (decoder L3-TC, STAGED global-d) — same
212	       // lock-step discipline. d0/d_coef/beta3 reach the kernel's P2.6 reduction;
213	       // inert/eager defaults (d_coef=1, beta3=0) for every non-Prodigy caller.
214	       d0, d_coef, beta3,
215	       // Muon append-only widening (ViT L3-TC, STAGED NS) — KEEP IN LOCK-STEP with
216	       // the real fused::sm90::FusedScalars (opt_components.cuh): same 3 trailing
217	       // fields, same order. The eager Muon's 1D-weight AdamW group has INDEPENDENT
218	       // hyperparameters (adamw_lr/adamw_betas, muon.py:115-125); these carry them
219	       // to the kernel's Muon P3 1D tail. Defaults = eager Muon adamw_* defaults;
220	       // every non-Muon caller leaves them untouched (only OptId::Muon's P3 reads).
221	       aux_lr, aux_beta1, aux_beta2,

223	       // backward) — KEEP IN LOCK-STEP with the real fused::sm90::FusedScalars
224	       // (opt_components.cuh): same 2 trailing fields, same order. rho = SAM
225	       // perturbation radius; looksam_sam = the every-k SAM-step gate (1.0 ⇒ run the
226	       // in-kernel perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g; 0.0 ⇒ reuse the cached

228	       rho, looksam_sam,
229	       // SuperGrok11/15 append-only widening (decoder/vit L3-TC, meta-net mu) — KEEP
230	       // IN LOCK-STEP with the real fused::sm90::FusedScalars (opt_components.cuh): two
231	       // trailing fields. sg_rescale = the SharpnessMetaNet rescale (mu = rescale·phi);

234	       // binds directly; only these scalars flow through the POD. Inert defaults
235	       // (sg_rescale=0.0, gate_temp=1.0) for every non-SG caller.

400	// Per-(device, n) reusable scratch for fused_step. The barrier counters and the
401	// `acts` proxy were previously reallocated (and `acts` memset over the full
402	// param size) on EVERY dispatch; sizes/offsets are constant for a given n.
403	// We persist them keyed by (device_index, n) and only reset the mutable parts
404	// (zero the 3 barrier counters + the acts buffer) per step. Behavior is
405	// identical — same zero-initialized scratch handed to the launcher — but the
406	// allocations/the full-size memset of sizes/offsets happen once per shape.
407	struct FusedScratch {
408	 torch::Tensor g_next;       // int32 [1]
409	 torch::Tensor g_arrived;    // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
410	 torch::Tensor g_generation; // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
411	 torch::Tensor sizes;        // int32 [1] = n  (constant per n)
412	 torch::Tensor offsets;      // int32 [1] = 0  (constant)
413	 torch::Tensor acts;         // float [numel(params)] proxy buffer
414	};
415	
416	// Keyed by (device_index, n). n disambiguates differing param shapes on the
417	// same device; acts is sized to params.numel() (== n here, single flat tensor).
418	inline FusedScratch& fused_scratch_for(const torch::Tensor& params, int64_t n) {
419	 static std::unordered_map<long long, FusedScratch> cache;
420	 const long long dev_idx =
421	 params.device().is_cuda() ? static_cast<long long>(params.device().index())
422	 : -1LL;
423	 const long long key = (dev_idx << 40) ^ static_cast<long long>(n);
424	 auto it = cache.find(key);
425	 if (it == cache.end()) {
426	 auto opts_i =
427	 torch::TensorOptions().device(params.device()).dtype(torch::kInt32);
428	 FusedScratch s;
429	 s.g_next = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
430	 s.g_arrived = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
431	 s.g_generation = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
432	 s.sizes = torch::full({1}, n, opts_i); // constant for this n
433	 s.offsets = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i); // constant
434	 s.acts = torch::zeros_like(params);
435	 it = cache.emplace(key, std::move(s)).first;
436	 } else {
437	 // Reset only the mutable scratch; sizes/offsets are invariant for this n.
438	 it->second.g_next.zero_();
439	 it->second.g_arrived.zero_();
440	 it->second.g_generation.zero_();
441	 it->second.acts.zero_();
442	 }
443	 return it->second;
444	}

580	// OptId int for the in-kernel optimizer TAIL, MIRRORING
581	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::OptId (kept as a local int map so this TU
582	// stays free of the device header — same discipline as the FusedScalars mirror).
583	// Returns the OptId for a SINGLE-LAUNCH wgmma-capable tail (no precompute stage, no
584	// 2nd backward, no sharpness ABI), or -1 for an optimizer whose L3-TC path needs more
585	// than the fwd+bwd+tail single launch (SG11/SG15/SG2). LookSAM IS now wired: its SAM
586	// 2nd backward is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4) — a perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g
587	// loop between B2 and P3, gated to every-k SAM steps — so it remains a SINGLE
588	// persistent launch (the same shape as Prodigy's P2.6 / Muon's P2.7 in-kernel stages).
589	// The owner-baseline directive routes exactly the -1!=... set onto the TC driver; the
590	// rest FAIL LOUD (here / in the Python gate) with their cited blocker.
591	static int wgmma_tail_opt_id(const std::string& optimizer) {
592	    if (optimizer == "adamw")      return 0;   // OptId::AdamW
593	    if (optimizer == "lion")       return 1;   // OptId::Lion
594	    if (optimizer == "grokfast")   return 2;   // OptId::Grokfast
595	    if (optimizer == "grokadamw")  return 3;   // OptId::GrokAdamW
596	    if (optimizer == "looksam")    return 4;   // OptId::LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd
597	                                               // backward — in-kernel P2.4 perturb→2nd
598	                                               // fwd+bwd→sam_dir, SINGLE persistent launch)
599	    if (optimizer == "prodigy")    return 5;   // OptId::Prodigy (STAGED global-d,
600	                                               // in-kernel P2.6 reduction — still a
601	                                               // SINGLE persistent launch)
602	    if (optimizer == "neuralgrok") return 6;   // OptId::NeuralGrok
603	    if (optimizer == "muon")       return 7;   // OptId::Muon (STAGED grid-cooperative
604	                                               // Newton-Schulz — in-kernel P2.7, still a
605	                                               // SINGLE persistent launch; vit wired)
606	    if (optimizer == "supergrok11") return 8;  // OptId::SuperGrok11 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd
607	                                               // backward → sharpness=(g_sam−g)² in P2.4 +
608	                                               // per-tensor meta-net mu/gate precompute in
609	                                               // P2.45; SINGLE persistent launch)
610	    if (optimizer == "supergrok15") return 9;  // OptId::SuperGrok15 (same SAM 2nd backward +
611	                                               // per-tensor mu precompute; gate is a host
612	                                               // scalar — SINGLE persistent launch)
613	    if (optimizer == "supergrok2")  return 10; // OptId::SuperGrok2 (FULL CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU
614	                                               // meta-net as the optimizer phase: in-kernel
615	                                               // SEGMENTED SORT (STAGE -1) + SAM 2nd backward
616	                                               // → sharpness + sg2_meta_stages; routed via the
617	                                               // DEDICATED mega_*_sg2_tc entry, NOT the generic
618	                                               // single-launch tail switch). Decoder/vit only;
619	                                               // mamba stays -1 (code-absent + A/A/A race).
620	    return -1;                                 // unroutable on the single-launch TC path
621	}
